messages:
incident-bot: ALERT triggered: kv-cache memory pressure across tp-pool-7, elevated paging and NCCL stalls detected. Severity: P1. Links: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/kv-cache-paging

sanjay: I’m paged, looking now. seeing high swap activity on nodes gpux-7..12 and NCCL timeouts in logs. hitting cache blowup after the 02:15 deploy.

maya: +1. customer-facing latencies spiking to 20s for chat completions. multiple tenants reporting tail latency regressions.

sanjay: quick summary: continuous-batching change from the deploy appears to change shard placement for kv cache in tensor-parallel mode. some shards ended up with 3x traffic -> fill and evict thrash -> memory pressure -> kernel swapping -> NCCL stalls.

alex: can we confirm which deploy? deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T02:15:03Z by maya -> feature/continuous-batching-v2 rolled to tp-serving (canary 5% -> 100%).

lucy: logs from gpux-9: ```
[03:02:17] kv_cache: shard=23 size=98% evict_rate=1200/s
[03:02:18] mm: swap_in=256MB/s swap_out=312MB/s
[03:02:19] nccl: op=AllReduce timeout after 12s
```

maya: workaround plan: 1) pause continuous batching (disable new config), 2) pin requests to legacy shard routing for tp-pool-7, 3) increase eviction aggressiveness, 4) rolling restart of gpux-7..12.

sanjay: agreed. immediate mitigation: hotfix to global config to set CONT_BATCHING_ENABLED=false and set MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024. I'll push hotfix.

alex: posting handoff to oncall-handoff channel and grabbing owner from infra. oncall-handoff: @sanjay starting incident lead.

sanjay: applying hotfix now. command: ```
kubectl set env deployment/tp-serving CONT_BATCHING_ENABLED=false -n inference
kubectl patch cm kv-cache-config -p '{"data":{"max_batch_tokens":"1024","eviction_threshold":"0.75"}}' -n inference
```

infra-bot: Patch applied to tp-serving config. Rolling restart of tp-serving replicas started.

maya: I’m pausing the rollout in the control plane and reverting the routing optimization (re-enable legacy consistent-hash). deploy-bot: rollback route change completed.

lucy: after config change and restart, gpux-9 swap activity dropped from 256MB/s to ~10MB/s within 30s. NCCL timeouts cleared on gpux-10 and gpux-11.

sanjay: notable: one host gpux-12 still showing high tail latency and evictions. hitting uneven partition: shard 7 assigned on gpux-12 with large KV prefix counts. investigating hotfix for shard rebalancer.

alex: can we temp move heavy prefixes to spillover? we have manual reassign API: ```
POST /admin/kv/reassign
{"from_shard":7,"to_shard":28,"keys":10000}
```

maya: do that for the worst prefixes. initiating small reassign to reduce pressure. will throttle to not induce NCCL re-sync storms.

infra-bot: reassign job created job_id=rb-20260315-01, throttling 50 keys/s.

lucy: reassign progress 40% on gpux-12, memory pressure modestly reducing. gpux-12 swap down to 48MB/s.

sanjay: monitoring. we should also adjust NCCL timeouts and enable async-progress to avoid stalls during rebalances. patching NCCL env on tp pool: ```
export NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
export NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=2
```

alex: customer-impact update: CS reported elevated error rates for customers A and B between 02:15-02:50 UTC, mostly timeouts and failed completions. notifying them with ETA for full remediation ~ 30m.

oncall-handoff: @sanjay handing off to @maya for post-mitigation monitoring window. leaving the thread at 03:05 UTC.

maya: monitoring window 20m started. so far tail latencies back to baseline for 85% of traffic. continuing rebalancer until gpux-12 stable.

lucy: found root cause hypothesis: new TP sharding algorithm in continuous-batching-v2 used a hash mix that depended on tokenization order, causing some prefixes to concentrate; under realistic traffic it caused hotspots. combined with reduced eviction headroom -> blowup.

sanjay: next actions: 1) revert sharding algorithm in repo (PR #4021), 2) add unit and stochastic tests for prefix distribution, 3) make continuous-batching rollout gradual with canary autoscale limit, 4) add metric for shard imbalance ratio and alert at 1.5x.

maya: filing postmortem ticket and scheduling war room review. will include customer impact timeline and mitigation playbook for kv-cache paging.

alex: team kudos for quick hotfix and safe reassign. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED at 1771009265. Root cause: TP KV-sharding regression in continuous-batching-v2 led to uneven partitioning -> cache thrash -> paging -> NCCL stalls. Mitigations: config hotfix, rolling restarts, shard reassignments, rollback of routing change, and NCCL env tuning. Follow-up: PM/Eng postmortem and test coverage.

maya: closing thread; will attach postmortem once written.
